angle: WR/TE route-cut force from Combine route drills (Break G), graded by the same code on NFL snaps, tested against full-season separation over expected (SOE) on held-out draft classes; last season's SOE as a priced day-3 tiebreaker; 2026 GO/HOLD calls.
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration (g, i.e. horizontal push as a share of body weight) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill and Combine year, reliability-shrunk; 1 sd = 0.021 g (about 4% of a typical 0.57 g drill cut).
headline_number: -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G [90%: -3.6, +1.0], n=116 receivers in unseen classes. Benefits above +1.0 and harms beyond -3.6 in are excluded at 5%; equivalence at +/-3 in is not shown; minimum detectable effect 3.5 in (80% power). Errors-in-variables version -1.2 [-3.9, +1.0]. None of the three mechanics carries signal (smallest Holm p 0.88). Day-3 tiebreak gain 0.31 [-0.08, 0.63], p 0.12; median 0.29 over 1,000 repeated receiver splits (positive in 85%). Rule pays while wrong on fewer than 64 of 100 disagreements; observed 34; cost if SOE were noise 0.2 in per call.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_18/cand_2. Football: draft metadata checked against nflverse (Tez Johnson 2025 R7-235 TB, Arian Smith 2025 R4-110 NYJ; all 116 slots match) and shown as round-pick in the calls table; a price for the day-3 rule (gain when right 17.2 in, loss when wrong 9.9 in, break-even 64 wrong per 100, observed 34, cost if SOE were noise 0.2 in = 0.03 catches; both candidates cost about the $1.08M minimum, so the price is production); appendix machinery cut to one robustness line; new per-receiver table of the 8 hardest and 8 softest drill cutters (drill Break G, NFL turn speed vs league with breaks, career SOE with routes); positive test of drill speed at the turn vs NFL speed at the turn on slants and outs (rho -0.06 [-0.27, 0.14], n=68) and a named protocol change (drill stems are entered faster than NFL cuts: hitch 6.9 vs 4.7, out 6.9 vs 5.4, in 8.0 vs 6.2 yd/s; cap the stem at game entry speed and add a second rep); games-missed flag on the persistence pairs (6 of 20 flagged; gain 0.44 without them). Data science: smallest margin the TOST rejects (3.6 in), MDE (3.5 in) and power at 3 in (0.69); Break G split into decel / speed through / re-acceleration with the same held-out test and Holm correction (all null, reliabilities 0.12, -0.04, 0.05); per-drill test-retest ICC (median 0.05 over 6 drills) and an errors-in-variables slope that rebuilds the shrinkage in every resample; 1,000 repeated receiver-split cross-validations of the day-3 gain. Writeup: plain two-sentence lede in inches, softened title, new 'What Break G measures' section in physical terms, one test and one p per claim, shuffle reconciliation, effective-n arithmetic, pick-gap-32 history, freeze/power detail and clip list removed; calls table reduced to Receiver, Call, True SOE [90%], What flips it; rule stated as a tiebreak only; speed reduced to 0.43 in the body. Viz: Fig 3 replaced by a tracking-native drill-vs-game path for Malik Washington's hitch (field x,y coloured by speed, plus speed traces); Fig 1 subtitle carries one message, panel B text enlarged, legend cut to two line styles with the league line annotated; Fig 2 gains the mechanics panel and the +/-3 in margin; Fig 4A shows the 15 day-3 WR pairs ranked and 4B carries the rule's price; Fig 5 GO/HOLD recoloured green/purple.
open_risks: The day-3 tiebreaker remains unproven (p 0.12; repeated-split 5th percentile -0.18); it is framed as a tiebreak lean only.
Equivalence at +/-3 in is still not shown and the MDE (3.5 in) is above the pre-set margin, so the null is inconclusive on harm.
Figure 3 and the per-receiver turn speeds rest on the sampled NFL plays (up to 40 per player, half top-EPA); Washington's path is one drill rep and one snap chosen by rule.
The protocol prescription (cap drill entry speed, add reps) is inferred from entry-speed gaps, not tested: no drill was run at NFL entry speed.
Per-drill test-retest ICCs rest on 59 repeat pairs across 6 drills; word count is near the limit (1,977).
